question: The US Government has recently announced its intention to further dismantle the International Criminal Court (ICC). At the same time, the European Union continues to support the court politically, legally and financially, despite recent integrity issues within the institution. 1.

In light of the recent announcements by the US Government and their implications for transatlantic relations, is the Commission prepared to reconsider or terminate cooperation between the European Union and the ICC? If not, why not?

How does the Commission assess the credibility of the ICC in light of the recent integrity issues surrounding former Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan, and is it prepared to commission an independent evaluation of the way in which the ICC has handled this matter and of the implications for the continuation of EU political, legal and financial support? If not, why not?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.8.2026) 1. The EU stands firm in its support for the International Criminal Court (ICC) and the principles set out in the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court. The EU considers that attacks or threats against the ICC, elected officials, personnel and those cooperating with the ICC are not acceptable.

The EU’s unwavering support for the international criminal justice system, including the ICC, has been most recently reaffirmed in the statement issued by the High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy and Vice-President of the European Commission on behalf of the EU on 16 July 2026, to mark the International Criminal Justice Day1. 2.

The EU is committed to preserving the ICC’s independence and integrity. The EU take note of the decision2 of the Assembly of State Parties to the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court following the disciplinary proceedings involving the ICC Chief Prosecutor. The EU have no further comments on this decision.
The EU also note that the Deputy Prosecutors have been in charge of managing the Office of the Prosecutor since 2025, ensuring business continuity of the ICC.
